config.rationale: A compact ResNet-style CNN with CIFAR-style 3x3 stride-1 stem (preserving 28x28 resolution), progressive channel expansion (64→128→256), and residual connections will effectively capture both local nuclear morphology and tissue-level texture in 28x28 histopathology patches. With ~2.8M parameters, it has sufficient capacity for 90k samples while fitting in limited GPU memory. Dataset-specific normalization and mild class weighting address the domain-specific color distribution and 1.63:1 imbalance. The residual architecture enables deeper feature hierarchies without vanishing gradients, and the global average pooling + dropout head provides regularization against overfitting on small patches.

representation.rationale: Standardization (zero-mean, unit-variance) is selected over unit-range scaling because the downstream architecture is a compact transformer operating on 16 patch tokens (7x7 non-overlapping patches on 28x28 RGB). Transformers are notably more sensitive to input magnitude than CNNs; centering each channel to zero mean and scaling to unit variance stabilizes attention logits and gradient flow, especially given the small per-channel stds (0.124, 0.177, 0.124) which would otherwise produce near-constant inputs after unit scaling. The channel means (0.741, 0.533, 0.706) confirm the data is already in [0,1], so standardization adds the critical centering step without distorting relative channel relationships in H&E staining. All six approved augmentations are applied train-only: hflip, vflip, rotate90, and rotate180 are orientation-safe for tissue-type labels (tissue morphology is rotation/flip invariant at the classification level), while brightness and contrast simulate inter-lab staining variability without altering structural content. This augmentation set maximizes effective training diversity on ~90k samples with mild class imbalance (1.63:1) without introducing geometric distortions that could confuse nuclear/cytoplasmic texture cues critical for distinguishing the 9 tissue classes.
